cases.purpose: tail -f prints the initial line, then each line a background writer appends; ^C ends the follow loop with the shell's SIGINT status and leaves no live writer
cases.oracle: parity vs GNU coreutils 9.7 tail run by the reference shell
cases.comparison: raw PTY output order checked by successive expects; exit status and tree compared
cases.script:
printf 'a
' > log
{ /usr/bin/sleep 0.4; printf 'b
' >> log; /usr/bin/sleep 0.4; printf 'c
' >> log; } &
tail -f log

cases.purpose: tail -F keeps following the name across a rename and recreate: a, b from the original file, then c, d from the new one; ^C ends it with status 130 (diagnostics discarded here, checked separately)
cases.oracle: parity vs GNU coreutils 9.7 tail run by the reference shell
cases.comparison: raw PTY output order by successive expects; exit status and tree compared
cases.script:
printf 'a
' > log
{ /usr/bin/sleep 0.5; printf 'b
' >> log; /usr/bin/sleep 0.5; mv log log.1; /usr/bin/sleep 0.6; printf 'c
' > log; /usr/bin/sleep 0.6; printf 'd
' >> log; } &
tail -F log 2>/dev/null

cases.purpose: tail -F on a file that does not exist yet waits and prints it once a writer creates it
cases.oracle: parity vs GNU coreutils 9.7 tail run by the reference shell
cases.comparison: raw PTY output by expect; exit status and tree compared
cases.script:
{ /usr/bin/sleep 0.6; printf 'x\n' > late; /usr/bin/sleep 0.4; printf 'y\n' >> late; } &
tail -F late 2>/dev/null

cases.purpose: The -F diagnostics for an initially missing file and for a rename/recreate, captured in a file and compared byte for byte with GNU tail
cases.oracle: parity vs GNU coreutils 9.7 tail run by the reference shell; the gaps between writer events (0.5-0.6 s) keep GNU's inotify message sequence stable
cases.comparison: exact bytes of the captured stderr file via tree parity; data order by expects
cases.script:
{ /usr/bin/sleep 0.6; printf 'a\n' > log; /usr/bin/sleep 0.6; mv log log.1; /usr/bin/sleep 0.6; printf 'c\n' > log; } &
tail -F log 2> diag
